subject: Effect of Covariates on scan1 output

messages.author: 69f7d832a0cbc260
messages.subject: Effect of Covariates on scan1 output
parts:
Dear Karl,

I am working on genetic mapping in a DO cohort and have been attempting to perform mediation analysis for a particular protein that I believe is causal for a LOD peak.

The way in which I have been doing this is as follows:
  • Add the protein abundance as a covariate in the cross2 object
  • Recalculate the genoprobs and alleleprobs
  • Use the alleleprobs object in scan1() and plot the output

Strangely, there was no effect on the LOD peaks after I had completed this process. I tried adding the covariate matrix explicitly into scan1 as well with addcovar, although this had no effect.

To test whether the covariates were having any effect, I removed all of the covariates (ngen, cage number and protein abundance) and recalculated files again. This had no effect on the scan1 output either. Please find attached screenshots of the scan1 outputs (grey is without covariates and blue is with).

Would you please be able to explain what is going wrong here?

Kind regards,

Harry

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Effect of Covariates on scan1 output
parts:
The covariate is going to have no effect on the genotype or allele probabilities. There is no need to re-calculate them.

You just need to include the protein as a covariate via addcovar in scan1().
I can't tell why it's not working. Maybe show the code that you are using.

karl

Hi Karl,

Thanks for your quick response.

I tried including covariates in scan1() again and it now seems to be working. I can't explain why this didn't work before, especially as I re-ran the same code. The only difference was that I didn't re-calculate the genotype probabilities first this time.

I now have another question regarding covariates. I would like to be able to include non-numerical covariates, such as cage number, into the analysis, as I have observed cage effects for some phenotypes. When I include these into addcovar, I receive the following error message "addcovar is not numeric". Would you please be able to suggest how I can include factor covariates into this analysis?

Would you also please be able to explain the purpose of intcovar as well?

Thanks in advance,

Harry

messages.author: d9fc134fd13e7e07
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Effect of Covariates on scan1 output
parts:
Hi, Harry,

When I've worked with data from DO mice, I've used batch covariates coded as a collection of binary indicator variables for all but one level of a factor. So, if I had k cages, I would use k-1 binary covariates. The i'th cage covariate, then, would have a one for the mice in cage i and zero for mice in other cages. 

If your cage covariate is a single character vector, cage_number, with distinct values corresponding to distinct cages, one way to code this in R is:

cage_number <- rep(paste0("cage", 1:4), each = 4) 
# i define above cage_number for illustration. you would just use your character vector and omit this line
unique(cage_number) -> levels
cage_binaries <- sapply(FUN = function(x)as.numeric(cage_number == x), X = as.list(levels))
cage_binaries

You could then use cage_binaries as an additive covariates matrix in calls to qtl2::scan1. Because qtl2::scan1 checks addcovar for linear independence and chooses a subset of columns that is linearly independent while maintaining the rank of the inputted matrix, you can actually input the full cage_binaries matrix without needing to first remove a column.

I believe that intcovar is for covariates that you wish to assess for genotype by covariate interactions, but I have less experience with that input.

In other words, I believe that qtl2::scan1, when called with non-NULL intcovar, models the trait Y as 

Y = (founder allele probabilities) + intcovar + intcovar * (founder allele probabilities) + epsilon

when you don't input a kinship matrix. If you input a kinship matrix, then you end up fitting the corresponding mixed effects model.

I hope that this helps.

fred

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Effect of Covariates on scan1 output
parts:
Another approach is to use model.matrix().

  # pull out the cage covariate and turn it into a factor
  cage <- factor(mycross$covar$cage)

  # use model.matrix to create a numeric matrix of 0/1 covariates
  cage_matrix <- model.matrix( ~ cage)

  # omit the first column; drop=FALSE ensures it stays as a matrix
  cage_matrix <- cage_matrix[,-1, drop=FALSE]

The main difficulty may be ensuring that the row names are preserved.

  rownames(cage_matrix) <- rownames(mycross$covar$cage)

karl
